Dowdy

DOW-dee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Dowdy is unfashionable and drab in appearance, especially in clothing.

The costume designer intentionally dressed the schoolteacher character in dowdy cardigans to contrast with the flashy lead actress.

Worked Example

The once-trendy shopping mall now looked dowdy, its faded signs and outdated storefronts untouched since the 1990s.

Nothing about the mall was stylish or up to date anymore -- it looked drab and old-fashioned, exactly what dowdy describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

frumpy: unfashionable and dull in appearance, especially clothing

drab: dull and lacking brightness or color

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

chic: stylish and fashionable

stylish: having a fashionable, attractive design

Where it sits · how run-down the look is — plain → dowdy → shabby

plain vs. dowdy: Something plain is simply simple and unadorned, not necessarily unfashionable the way dowdy clothing is.

shabby vs. dowdy: Something shabby is worn-out and threadbare, an even more run-down look than merely dowdy.

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Dowdy's exact origin is genuinely uncertain -- dictionaries trace it only as far back as an obsolete word 'dowd,' used for a plain, dully dressed woman, with no clear root beyond that.

Use the root in a new word: dowd

Use the root in a new word: dowd: Old etiquette guides sometimes warned young women against becoming a 'dowd' who never bothered with fashion.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Dowdy is about being unfashionable and drab, not necessarily untidy -- clothing can be perfectly neat and clean and still look dowdy, which sets it apart from unkempt (messy and uncared for) or tousled (playfully disordered).
